summary: @galicia-toolkit-nestjs/paas exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials to oob.s4yhii.com on require()
details: On require('@galicia-toolkit-nestjs/paas'), index.js unconditionally loads a native addon at prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node inside a try/catch that silently swallows load errors. The ELF addon has no legitimate metrics functionality; it reads credential-grade environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN) together with hostname, user, and cwd, forks and setsids to detach from the parent, and POSTs the collected data as JSON to the hardcoded host oob.s4yhii.com (HTTP/1.0 POST /native, Content-Type: application/json). The JS layer presents a benign NestJS shim (forRoot/createLogger stubs) as a cover story while the payload is smuggled inside the native binary. The package version (999.0.4), scope resembling a legitimate toolkit namespace, UNLICENSED metadata, and generic 'metrics' addon naming are consistent with a dependency-confusion credential stealer targeting CI runners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
